arxiv-2106-01033.title: Who Blames or Endorses Whom? Entity-to-Entity Directed Sentiment Extraction in News Text Thanks: This work was done while the first author was a postdoctoral researcher at UCLA.
arxiv-2106-01033.creator: Kunwoo Park, Zhufeng Pan, Jungseock Joo
arxiv-2106-01033.description: Abstract Understanding who blames or supports whom in news text is a critical research question in computational social science. Traditional methods and datasets for sentiment analysis are, however, not suitable for the domain of political text as they do not consider the direction of sentiments expressed between entities.

arxiv-2106-09147.creator: Wenjie Fang
arxiv-2106-09147.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Wenjie Fang. Initiated by Davis, Nelson, Petersen and Tenner (2018), the enumerative study of pinnacle sets of permutations has attracted a fair amount of attention recently. In this article, we provide a recurrence that can be used to compute efficiently the number | 𝔖 n ​ ( P ) | |\mathfrak{S}_{n}(P)| of permutations of size n n with a given pinnacle set P P , with arithmetic complexity O ⁡ ( k 4 + k ​ log ⁡ n ) O(k^{4}+k\log n) for P

arxiv-2108-08821.title: Performance comparison of CFD-DEM solver MFiX-Exa, on GPUs and CPUs
arxiv-2108-08821.creator: Shandong Lao, Aaron Holt, Deepthi Vaidhynathan, Hariswaran Sitaraman, Christine M. Hrenya, Thomas Hauser
arxiv-2108-08821.description: Abstract We present computational performance comparisons of gas-solid simulations performed on current CPU and GPU architectures using MFiX Exa, a CFD-DEM solver that leverages hybrid CPU+GPU parallelism. A representative fluidized bed simulation with varying particle numbers from 2 to 67 million is used to compare serial and parallel performance.

arxiv-2109-11981.title: Multipartite Generalization of Geometric Measure of Discord
arxiv-2109-11981.creator: Ali Saif M. Hassan, Pramod S. Joag
arxiv-2109-11981.description: Abstract Radhakrishnan et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 124, 110401 (2020)] proposed a generalization of quantum discord to multipartite systems, which is consistent with the conventional deﬁnition of discord in bipartite systems, and derived explicit formulae for any multipartite state. These results are significant in capturing quantum correlations for multi-qubit systems.

arxiv-2111-08359.title: A change of measure formula for recursive conditional expectations
arxiv-2111-08359.creator: Luca Di Persio, Alessandro Gnoatto, Marco Patacca
arxiv-2111-08359.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Luca Di Persio, Alessandro Gnoatto, Marco Patacca. We derive a representation for the value process associated to the solutions of forward-backward stochastic differential equations in a jump-diffusion setting under multiple probability measures. Motivated by concrete financial problems, the latter representations are then applied to devise a generalization of the change of numéraire technique allowing to obtain recursive pricing formulas in the presence of non-linear funding terms due to e.g. collateralization agreements.

arxiv-2204-07412.title: End-to-End Sensitivity-Based Filter Pruning
arxiv-2204-07412.creator: Zahra Babaiee, Lucas Liebenwein, Ramin Hasani, Daniela Rus, Radu Grosu
arxiv-2204-07412.description: Abstract In this paper, we present a novel sensitivity-based filter pruning algorithm (SbF-Pruner) to learn the importance scores of filters of each layer end-to-end. Our method learns the scores from the filter weights, enabling it to account for the correlations between the filters of each layer.

arxiv-2310-01971.description: Abstract In the last two decades, the sequential optimality conditions, which do not require constraint qualifications and allow improvement on the convergence assumptions of algorithms, had been considered in the literature. arxiv-2401-15548.description: Abstract The hot-Neptune desert is one of the most sparsely populated regions of the exoplanet parameter space, and atmosphere observations of its few residents can provide insights into how such planets have managed to survive in such an inhospitable environment.

arxiv-2407-18765.title: Strong chain control sets and affine control systems
arxiv-2407-18765.creator: Fritz Colonius, Alexandre J. Santana
arxiv-2407-18765.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Fritz Colonius, Alexandre J. Santana. For control-affine systems on non-compact manifolds, the notion of strong chain control sets is introduced and related to the strong chain transitivity of the associated control flows. Affine control systems on ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} are embedded into bilinear control systems in an extended state space and it is shown that they are topologically conjugate to the induced system on the northern hemisphere of the Poincaré sphere. This preserves strong chain control sets.

arxiv-2503-01472.title: Transferring between Sparse and Dense Matching via Probabilistic Reweighting PubID: pubid: 0000–0000/00$00.00 © 2021 IEEE
arxiv-2503-01472.creator: Ya Fan, Rongling Lang
arxiv-2503-01472.description: Abstract Detector-based and detector-free matchers are only applicable within their respective sparsity ranges. To improve the adaptability of existing matchers, this paper introduces a novel probabilistic reweighting method. Our method is applicable to Transformer-based matching networks and adapts them to different sparsity levels without altering network parameters. The reweighting approach adjusts attention weights and matching scores through feature detection probabilities.

arxiv-2512-22305.title: PDx—Adaptive Credit Risk Forecasting Model in Digital Lending using Machine Learning Operations
arxiv-2512-22305.creator: Sultan Amed, Chan Yu Hang, Sayantan Banerjee
arxiv-2512-22305.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sultan Amed, Chan Yu Hang, Sayantan Banerjee. This paper presents PDx, an adaptive, machine learning operations (MLOps) driven decision system for forecasting credit risk using probability of default (PD) modeling in digital lending. While conventional PD models prioritize predictive accuracy during model development with complex machine learning algorithms, they often overlook continuous adaptation to changing borrower behaviour, resulting in static models that degrade over time in production and generate inaccurate default predictions.

arxiv-2512-24691.title: Non-perturbative Thermodynamics of Quark Gluon Plasma and Gravitational Waves
arxiv-2512-24691.creator: Narasimha Reddy Gosala, Arundhati Dasgupta
arxiv-2512-24691.description: Abstract Quark–Gluon Plasma (QGP), a strongly interacting state of the early universe, exhibits remarkably fluid-like behavior despite its underlying non-Abelian dynamics. Motivated by these features, we explore time-dependent S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) SU(2) Yang–Mills condensates as non-linear classical background fields to model QGP.

pmc-12562775.title: Epithelial-Immune Cell Crosstalk in Salivary Gland Tumors: Implications for Tumor Progression and Diagnostic Assessment
pmc-12562775.creator: Martina Sausa, Giuseppe Vergilio, Rosario Barone, Rossana Porcasi, Prince Ofori, Fatima Azhraa Haddad, Francesca Rappa, Francesca Levi-Schaffer, Angelo Leone
pmc-12562775.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study explores immunophenotypic and angiogenic profiles in salivary gland tumors (SGTs), focusing on epithelial–mesenchymal dynamics and immune–stromal interactions. Immunohistochemical analysis of E-cadherin, Vimentin, mast cell tryptase (MCT), CD300a, CK18, CD31, and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) was performed in normal salivary tissue, pleomorphic adenomas (PA), and squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) to assess epithelial plasticity, mast cell (MC) involvement, and vascular remodeling. Normal glands showed compartmentalized E-cadherin (epithelial) and Vimentin (mesenchymal) expression, with stromal MCs positive for MCT and CD300a.

pmc-12715623.description: The biological role of DNA and RNA G-quadruplexes (G4s) is relayed to the cellular circuitry by a plethora of proteins known as G4-binding proteins (G4PBs).
